svg.text: Light is the only cliff this register can prove.
anyone about to read a community claim off a depth slice
whether a depth band's mix is biology or one ship's itinerary
the deep bands keep their composition once the largest dataset
what share of each depth bin belongs to each group
ratio to the same group's share of the top 20 m, log scale
its share of this bin ÷ its share of 0-20 m
Every line starts at 1.0 by construction. The photosynthesisers cross 0.1
within 70 m and bottom out between 0.00043 and 0.0024 — three decades down.
The controls never leave the 0.1 to 1.0 decade at any depth on this panel.
Stony corals are the intermediate the panel was built to contain, with a
floor of 0.092, because reef corals carry photosynthetic symbionts and
and where that ratio stops meaning anything
largest dataset's share of each depth band; area is records in the band
biggest single dataset's share of the band
under 25% — a share here is a measurement
The light cliff sits at 20–50 m, where 1,189–2,665 datasets contribute and
the largest holds 9–12%. The other cliff worth hunting was the carbonate
compensation depth near 4,500 m, and forams do fall from 2.04% of the 3–4 km
band to 0.39% of the 4–5 km band — right size, right place. It cannot be
claimed: sea cucumbers are 26.7% of that band by themselves. Blocked, not
OBIS v3 statistics/env, /occurrence and /dataset, fetched 2026-09-18. The 38 depth bins are NOT equal width — 10 m to 200 m, then 100 m, then 1,000 m
— so the raw histogram's steps at 200 m and 1,000 m are the bin widening, not a boundary: per metre, 190–200 m holds 67,390 records and 200–300 m
holds 45,865, a fall drawn as a rise. Only the 10 m bins are used here. startdepth/enddepth match a record's depth RANGE, so abutting bands overlap
and their counts must not be summed; every band figure is a ratio inside one query. Bathymetry, sst, sss and shoredistance are on every record but
cannot be filtered on — those params return the unfiltered total, exactly as a nonsense param does.
